newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian communists rally on revolution anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Russian communists rally on revolution anniversary.

text.p: Thousands of communists marched under red banners in central Moscow and other cities in Russia on Thursday to commemorate the 79th anniversary of the Bolshevik revolution.

Several thousand people, most of them elderly, gathered in central Moscow to hear Communist Party leader Gennady Zyuganov criticise President Boris Yeltsin, who is recovering after his open heart surgery two days ago.
Zyuganov said the 23-hour transfer of Yeltsin's powers to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin while he had the operation and came round had made Russia a laughing stock.

"This spectacle of a one-day president for 23 hours has made us a laughing stock in the eyes of the world community," said Zyuganov, who lost to Yeltsin in the second round of this year's presidential election.
The communists then marched through the centre of Moscow but were not allowed to cross Red Square.
Soviet leaders used to celebrate the anniversary, which brought communists to power, with a huge parade on Red Square.

On the major day in the Soviet calender, the Communist Party's ruling Politburo used to watch the marches from the top of Soviet state founder Vladimir Lenin's mausoleum under the Kremlin's red fortress walls.
Rallies were also taking place in other cities across Russia but it was not immediately known how many people had taken part.
Yeltsin issued a decree on Thursday renaming Revolution Day as the Day of Accord and Reconciliation. The decree ensured that November 7 would remain a holiday.
News of Yeltsin's decree came too late for any immediate reaction from the commuist leaders.
